newsitem.title: USA: US government denies oil pollution act accusations.
newsitem.headline: US government denies oil pollution act accusations.

text.p: The U.S. government Wednesday denied the key allegations in a lawsuit filed by Maritrans Inc seeking $200 million in compensation for double-hull requirements imposed under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990.
But the government did not ask for a quick dismissal of the case, which was filed in August.
In its response, the government denied it had "taken" the company's property or had taken it without just compensation, as barred by the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution.
The company had argued that 37 of its oil-carrying barges had been "taken" in the sense that the value of their useful lives had been reduced to about 15 years from about 50 years.
"(T)o the extent that the allegation may be deemed an allegation of fact, it is denied," the Justice Department said in the Clinton administration's response.
"Now the case will just proceed along," said Arthur Volkle, associate general counsel for Maritrans.
The next move would likely entail setting a "discovery schedule" for the two sides, he said.
The Oil Pollution Act, passed in the wake of the Exxon Valdez disaster, called for all tank vessels in U.S. waters to have double hulls by 2015, phasing in the rule from 1995.
Industry attorneys said that if Maritrans was successful, the case could spawn a pile of similar cases.
